claims.text: Overall tribo-corrosion degradation in HEAs is governed by a dynamic, self-healing tribolayer that is continuously disrupted by sliding.
Rapid reformation of the tribolayer and its protection of the substrate determine the balance between wear and corrosion.
An HEA containing Cr, Al, or similar passivating elements can form a stable native oxide under static conditions.
The microstructure and composition of a dynamically formed near-surface layer mediate its stability and resistance to mechanical disruption.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface structure can contribute to low friction and high wear resistance in an HEA.
Sliding mechanically removes portions of the protective passive film and exposes fresh metal.
Freshly exposed metal rapidly re-oxidizes during sliding in a corrosive environment.
Favorable alloying and nanoscale grain structure enhance passive-film reformation and mechanical integrity.
A mechanically robust, rapidly reforming film reduces wear by minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact.
Rapid film reformation reduces corrosion by quickly re-establishing a barrier.
Composition modification can improve both wear and corrosion resistance in an HEA.
An HEA optimized for passivation will have lower total mass loss than a matched baseline lacking that optimization.
The passivation-optimized HEA will have lower corrosion current density than the baseline during the controlled comparison.
The passivation-optimized HEA will have a lower wear rate than the baseline during the controlled comparison.
More effective passive-film reformation will mitigate catastrophic localized corrosion under sliding.
The prediction should hold at moderate loads and in corrosive environments where passivation is kinetically feasible.
The proposed mechanism may fail when mechanical removal is faster than passive-film reformation.
The proposed passivation mechanism may fail under inert conditions because oxidation and mixed metal-oxide film formation are suppressed.
Two otherwise matched HEAs, with and without passivating-element enrichment, can be compared under identical ball-on-disk conditions in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
A failure to obtain statistically lower wear and corrosion or a failure of tribolayer dynamics to correlate with degradation reduction would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
